Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:11: And sometimes the light that descends becomes depicted in the imaginative faculty in the likeness of an angel speaking with him, and he sees it or hears its voice, and the like, through one of the five known faculties of the soul within the imaginative faculty, and from there they are transferred to their outer counterparts, the five [physical] senses, which likewise come from the animal soul, as is known — and then he actually sees, hears, smells, and speaks with his physical senses. And as it is written (II Samuel 23:2), "the spirit of the Lord spoke through me, and His word was on my tongue," for that light becomes materialized and depicted in the physical senses; and sometimes his prophecy will be in the five spiritual senses that are within his imaginative faculty alone. And all this occurs through the imaginative faculty's becoming entirely detached from all thoughts of matter, as mentioned:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:12: It follows that prophecy is like a dream in this respect, that his intellective soul leaves him and ascends above, level by level, and there it beholds and observes, and afterward returns and descends and imparts this light down to the animal soul, in which is the imaginative faculty, and there those matters become depicted and materialized still further; and when the person awakens, his soul remembers those matters through the retentive faculty and the memory faculty, which are likewise in the animal soul, as is known in the science of nature.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:13: And thus the matter of prophecy and the matter of the dream have both been well explained: the latter occurs while the soul is in the body, the former after the soul has departed. Indeed, prophecy itself is of two kinds,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:14: one is the prophecy of the other prophets, in which, at the time the light is drawn down and reaches, in its descent, the intellective soul within him, and from there descends to the animal soul to be depicted there in the five inner senses within the imaginative faculty — the outer, physical senses would tremble with great trembling and would fall down, for they have no power to receive that light and depict it and materialize it in the physical senses. And prophecy of this kind is called a "dream," even though it is not an actual dream, as mentioned (Genesis 15:12), "and a deep sleep fell upon Abram," and so on:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:15: And the second kind is complete prophecy, in which the physical senses did not tremble at all, and the matters were depicted within him calmly — and this was the prophecy of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and the reason for this was that he was entirely refined in matter, and was transformed, through the holiness of his deeds, to be at the level of the soul, for his venom was removed and only the good and refined part remained in his body, and likewise in the faculties of his yesodit soul, for only in them is there an aspect of physicality, and not in the intellective soul and above:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:16: And it has already been explained that there are roots without end for the soul of man. Now, according to the level of the source of its quarry, so does the power of drawing down the abundance of his prophecy grow great. And likewise, even if the root of the quarry of his soul is at a supernal place, but he did not rectify and did not merit to draw down [abundance] from all the roots from there downward, then he too cannot draw down the abundance of his prophecy except from that level which he did rectify and merit to reach, and from there alone the abundance of his prophecy is drawn; and by this you will understand how many levels there are among the prophets, without end:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:17: And do not think that, since we have explained that the soul of the prophet does not leave his body, there is then no actual grasp at all in his thought to ascend to open the gates, and so on — this you will understand from what I wrote above, that the soul is like a very long branch, extending from the root attached to the tree down to the body of the man. And that continuous line, while the person yearns to ascend to his root, the light of his thought — called the muskal (the thing intellectually grasped) from the maskil (the intellect that grasps) — ascends, that is, the soul that grasps intellectually, up to the very sechel (intellect), which is the supernal root of his soul, and they cleave together and become one through the very act of intellection itself, which is the abundance drawn from the sechel to the maskil. It follows that the muskal is the very light and abundance itself descending from the sechel to the grasping soul, and this abundance and actual light is the matter called "thought" — and understand this well, for it is not an empty thing, for if it were not so, this would nullify all the matters of the intentions of prayers and the good and bad musings of a person:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:18: And thus it has been well explained to you that prophecy is necessarily bound to exist and can be — like the matter of a person grasping in his hand the tip of a branch of a tree while it is bent downward, and shaking it with force, so that the entire tree necessarily shakes; but the supernal beings will not be shaken by the thought of the lower man except when he is fit to draw the supernal light upon them, and then, with this joy, they too will draw down some of that light upon him. But if he has no power to draw supernal light upon them, they will not regard him at all, and will not consent to draw near to help him and to draw his thought upward, for it is vanity and has no benefit in it:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:1-4: What is the nature of the prophecy of the early generations, and what is the nature of the attainment of the Holy Spirit that is possible to attain even in our own time:

And the matter of the prophecy of the prophets is as follows: for it has been explained above how there are four worlds called Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Assiyah, and below all of them is the lowly world, which divides into four elements, namely, the faculties of their yesodit souls, and they divide in the manner of ten sefirot.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:5: It has also been explained that in every world there is an inner light, which is the ten sefirot, and outer to them the light of the quarry of the souls, and outer to it the light of the quarry of the angels, and outer to it a dark light, the quarry of the kelipot, and outer to it the world itself, which is the firmaments of that world; and it is exactly the same in the lowly world, for the matter of the four elements is the "body" and the "world," and within it are the other lights, each one of them composed of the four aspects of the yesodit soul.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:6: It has also been explained that there are levels without end, for a sefirah is composed of ten, and ten of ten, and so on, in such a way that every world has levels without end:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:7: And the quality of prophecy has already been explained in Gate Five: that the thought of the prophet extends and ascends level by level, from below to above, until it reaches the place where the root of his soul is attached, and then he would think to elevate the light of the sefirot up to the Ein Sof, and draw down light from there, and then bring it back down from above to below, through the levels by which he had ascended, until it reaches down to his intellective soul, and it takes its portion in that light according to the measure of the attachment of the root of his soul above, and from there it draws it down, by the imaginative faculty, into the animal soul within him, and there those matters become depicted in the inner senses within the imaginative faculty, or in the outer senses:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:8: And the drawing down of that thought was certainly not ascending of itself, but rather through intentions (kavvanot) and unifications (yichudim) handed down to him by the prophet who taught him to prophesy, as with the sons of the prophets alongside Samuel, Elijah, and Elisha, of blessed memory, so that through those unifications which he would perform, he would draw down the light and the abundance according to his will — this is the ultimate purpose of the matter of prophecy:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:9: There were also further things they would teach them, namely, prayers and mentions of Names to the guardians of the gates of the firmaments and of the chambers in every single world, from the ends of the worlds — namely the four elements and the airs within them — up to the height of the World of Atzilut, as mentioned in Sefer HaZohar, Parashat Vayakhel, regarding the ascent of prayers (201b), and as mentioned in the chapters of the Heichalot and their beraitot; and at first they would use [these] to open the gates at that level, and afterward they would perform the unification and the prayer particular to that level, and so they would ascend from level to level, until they reached their supernal root and rested there. And afterward they would extend their thoughts still further, up to the Ein Sof, and then return and draw the abundance down below, as mentioned above:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:10: And the matter of these gatekeepers and these Names, their meaning is this: they would adjure, by the power of one holy Name, which is from the sefirah at that level, the angel rooted and hewn from there, who is appointed over the gate of the firmament itself, which is the matter at that level, who also has his own known name for that gate, and open it; and then the prophet's thought would enter through that gate, from light to light, until the inner light of the sefirah at that level, and then he would pray and perform the unification necessary for that place, and so he would ascend from level to level:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:11: And this is the matter of Ezekiel's visions, called Ma'aseh Merkavah (the Account of the Chariot), since the levels are structured one upon another. And first the heavens were opened — the gates of the firmaments, which are the lights of the matter and the vessels of that world — and from there he entered into the kelipot, and this is what is written (Ezekiel 1:4), "and I looked, and behold, a stormy wind," and so on,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:12: and as it is written in Hosea (1:2), "the beginning of the word of the Lord through Hosea" — meaning, at the beginning of the revelation of the speech of prophecy, the kelipah and its powers were revealed first, which are "a wife of harlotry" and "children of harlotry."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:13: And indeed, while he was in the heavens, there too he would cleave and gaze, as it is written (Ezekiel 1:1), "the heavens were opened and I saw visions of God"; but when he reached the place of the kelipot, he took no pleasure in cleaving to them, but rather passed through and over them, and did not cling to them, only a necessary, incidental glance. And this is the mystery of Elijah, of blessed memory (I Kings 19:12), "not in the wind is the Lord... not in the fire is the Lord," and so on.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:14: And from there he entered into the domain of the light of the angels, as is known, for between every light and every light there is a curtain (pargod) separating them, and this is the hidden mystery contained in the matter of chashmal (the electrum), for it equals, by gematria, malbush (garment), and it is the vessel and matter of the lights of the angels — and may the Lord forgive me for this hidden secret I have revealed.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:15: And then he saw ten classes of angels, all of whom divide into four living creatures and four camps of the Shechinah, and this is what is written (Ezekiel 1:5), "and from its midst, the likeness of four living creatures," and from there he entered until he reached the light of the ten sefirot themselves, and this is what is written (ibid., v. 26), "and above the likeness of the throne was the likeness, as the appearance of a man," and so on. And indeed the throne itself is the light of the quarry of the souls, in the mystery of "the Patriarchs, they themselves are the Chariot," and therefore the soul is called kavod (glory), as it is written (Psalms 30:13), "so that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent," and it is written (Psalms 4:3), "how long shall my glory be turned into shame," and so on:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:16: And behold, I have revealed to you a deep secret, encompassing the matters of the Chariot, which the earlier generations before us did not merit. And it has already been explained above, in Gate Five, that not all the prophets nurse from a single root, for they have roots without end, and there are six hundred thousand of them in every world. And this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:62, 92), six hundred thousand prophets arose in Israel, and so on, and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, includes them all and is weighed as equal to them all:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:17: And in a general manner let us explain their level: for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, would ascend to Atzilut and from there see actually — except that this was through his clothing himself in Beriah alone, and even this only by way of passing through, for Atzilut itself is impossible [to reach directly], and this is the mystery of (Exodus 33:20), "for man shall not see Me and live"; and the rest of the prophets would see into Atzilut through complete clothing in the lights of Beriah:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:18: And after the destruction, came Ezekiel, who prophesied from Atzilut after its clothing in Beriah, and Beriah in Yetzirah, in complete clothing, and from then on no light of Atzilut or Beriah is revealed at all. And to this our Sages, of blessed memory, referred (Sotah 48b; Sanhedrin 11a): after [the deaths of] Chaggai, Zechariah, and Malachi, prophecy ceased entirely, and only the Holy Spirit remained — this being the continued extension of the lights of Yetzirah itself alone, and from there downward; and this is called, in the Talmud (Chagigah 14b), the "ascent to the Pardes," which is Yetzirah, called the world of Metatron; and for this too there were known usages to open the gates that exist from the lowly world and Assiyah and Yetzirah, and to perform the unifications and the prayers appropriate to the World of Yetzirah, in its ten sefirot:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:19: And this is the mystery of the practice of the chapters of the Heichalot, which Rabbi Nechunya, Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Yishmael, and the Men of the Great Assembly made use of, and afterward even the ways of those usages were forgotten. And there is a further reason: that the purity of the ashes of the [red] heifer was lost in the time of the Amoraim, until the time of Abaye and Rava, as mentioned in the Talmud (Chagigah 25), and therefore, from then on, they no longer made use of the ascent to the Pardes.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:20: And from then on they made use only of the usages of the World of Assiyah alone, and since it is the lowest world of all, and also since the angels within it are a minority good and a majority evil, and moreover the good and the evil are very closely bound together within it, therefore there is no attainment through it at all that is pure, for it is impossible to attain the good alone, and therefore the attainment is mixed with good and evil, truth and falsehood:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:21: And this is the mystery of the matter of "practical Kabbalah," and therefore it is forbidden to make use of it, for one will necessarily become attached also to the evil that is bound up with the good, and though he thinks to purify his soul, he defiles it because of that evil; and even if he does attain something, it is truth mixed with falsehood, and especially since the ashes of the [red] heifer are no longer available, and the impurity of the kelipot clings to the person who draws near to attain through practical Kabbalah; therefore let one who guards his soul stay far from them, for besides defiling his soul, he will be punished in Gehinnom, and even in this world we have a tradition that either he or his offspring will become impoverished, or he or his offspring will fall ill with sicknesses, or he or his offspring will apostatize:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:22: And take proof from Rabbi Yosef della Reina and Rabbi Shlomo Molcho, who made use of practical Kabbalah and were lost from the world, and all this for the reason mentioned, that there is no good without evil, and moreover, that they compel these [forces] against their will through adjurations, and then they entice them and turn them toward bad paths until they destroy their souls,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 6:23: and greater still than this is the fact that the earlier ones concealed all these ways of adjuration, and we are not well versed in their ways, and it is fitting to keep entirely far from them:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 7:1-3: On the conduct of the Holy Spirit in our own time:

After we have warned man, in the preceding gate, about all the ways of attainment mentioned above, let a person not despair. For regarding the verse (Judges 4:4), "and Deborah, a woman, a prophetess" — it was taught in the school of Elijah: I call heaven and earth to witness for me, whether man or woman, whether gentile or Jew, whether slave or maidservant — all according to a person's deeds, the Holy Spirit rests upon him:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 7:4: And indeed, with our own ears we have heard, and with our own eyes we have seen, rare and select individuals who attained the level of the Holy Spirit even in our own time, and they would foretell future things, and among them were possessors of wisdom that had not been revealed in the generations before us; and so as not to weaken the hands of those who come to draw near to sanctify themselves, I shall explain some matters and open, as it were, the eye of a needle's crack, and may the good Lord not withhold good from those who walk in innocence. And first let us explain several matters concerning the attainment, and in the Eighth Gate I shall write the order of conduct for them, with the help of the blessed Lord:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 7:5: Behold, the choicest of all paths is what we have written in the name of the school of Elijah, of blessed memory, and it is the path the early pious ascetics practiced. And it is this: to return in powerful repentance from everything he has corrupted, and afterward to complete his soul through the fulfillment of positive commandments, and with the utmost intention in his prayers, and in engaging in Torah lishmah with alacrity, like an ox to the yoke, until his strength is spent, and with a minimum of pleasures, eating, and drinking, and with rising at midnight or a little less, and with distancing himself from all unseemly character traits, and with abstaining from all people, even in matters of idle conversation; and afterward he should purify his body through constant immersion, and afterward he should seclude himself at times and reflect upon the fear of the Lord, and set the Name Havayah before his eyes always, and take care that his thought be free of all the vanities of this world, and cleave to His love, blessed be He, with great longing — and through this it is possible that he may merit the Holy Spirit through one of these modes, as follows:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 7:6: The first is that he draws down upon his soul a supernal light from the root of his supernal soul, as mentioned above in Gate Five, and it is revealed to him, and this is the complete Holy Spirit:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 7:7: The second is that through his engagement in Torah, or his fulfillment of some commandment mentioned in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory (Avot ch. 4, mishnah 11), whoever performs a single commandment acquires for himself one advocate, and an actual angel is created from it — but on condition that he fulfill it constantly and with great intention, as required — then that angel will be revealed to him. And this is the matter of what is found written in books regarding angels called maggidim ("tellers"), except that if the commandment was not performed as required, that maggid will be mixed with good and evil, truth and falsehood:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 7:8: The third is that through piety, as mentioned above, Elijah, of blessed memory, will be revealed to him, and according to his piety will his revelation grow:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 7:9: The fourth is greater than all of them, and it is that he merits that the soul of one of the deceased righteous ones is revealed to him, whether from among those who are from the root of his own soul, as is known, or from others, simply because he performed some commandment properly, as did that righteous one. And whoever merits this level will attain that they make known to him wisdoms and hidden secrets of the Torah, to a wondrous degree, all according to his deeds:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 7:10: The fifth, and the lowest of all, is that he will see in his dreams matters of the future and wisdom close to the Holy Spirit:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 7:11: Now, this way is the straight way, for since the person does not adjure or compel the supernal beings, but only through the power of his good deeds and his holiness, certainly the pure Holy Spirit will rest upon him without any admixture of evil at all — which is not so when a person compels or seeks ways of adjuration through deeds, prayers, and unifications, for if he errs in them at all, it is possible that external, mixed things may come his way:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 7:12: There are also other ways, through action, and I shall explain them in the Fourth Part — namely, to draw down upon himself one of the five modes mentioned, even if they do not come of themselves — but these require great holiness and purity, so that there be no admixture as mentioned. However, the first way was practiced even in the earlier generations, as Nachmanides, of blessed memory, wrote regarding the verse (Deuteronomy 11:22, 30:20), "and to cleave to Him," and in the Iggeret HaKodesh which he composed, in the fifth chapter, regarding the matter of Ben Azzai, who sat and studied while the fire blazed all around him:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 8:1-3: To explain, in a very brief manner, the conduct of one who comes to sanctify himself in our own time:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 8:4: The first: he must return from all his sins, whether in negative commandments, or in neglecting the fulfillment of positive commandments, or in any words of the Rabbis, or in every kind of unseemly character trait, and never return to them again — and especially from all transgressions liable to karet and death, and desecration of the Name, and in the observance of the Sabbath, and from niddah and every kind of seminal emission, and from an oath even if true, and from gazing at forbidden sights, and from evil speech, and from gossip-mongering, and from mockery, and from idle talk; and he should distance himself from pride, anger, touchiness, and sadness, and should conduct himself with humility and lowliness, and be glad with his lot:
